name: Formal prepositions: due to, owing to, in view of, regardless of
subtitle: In reports, letters and news you often meet prepositions made of several words, such as due to, in view of and regardless of. They are followed by a noun or an -ing form, not by a clause. If you need a clause, add the fact that.

flow.text: due to, in view of, despite, regardless of …

concept.exampleHtml: In view of the high costs, the council has delayed the new library. · The delay was due to bad weather. · Despite the fact that it rained, the match went ahead.

qa.html: Reason: due to, owing to, on account of, as a result of mean "because of". In view of and in the light of mean "taking this situation into account". The flight was delayed owing to fog. In view of the weather, the match was cancelled.

Contrast: despite and in spite of mean "although there is". Regardless of and irrespective of mean "it does not matter": Everyone can enter, regardless of age. Notwithstanding is very formal and found mostly in legal texts: The plan went ahead, notwithstanding the objections.

Topic, method, role: with regard to and in terms of name the topic (In terms of cost, plan B is better.). On behalf of means "for someone". By means of means "using". In accordance with means "following" (rules, a contract). Prior to means "before". In addition to and apart from add or exclude something.

These prepositions take a noun or an -ing form. They cannot take a clause with its own subject and verb. If you want a clause, put the fact that after the preposition: due to the rain or due to the fact that it rained. After be, use due to: The delay was due to snow. (Owing to usually starts a sentence or a phrase.)

Typical mistakes: ✗ Despite of the rain, we went out. → ✓ Despite the rain / In spite of the rain (only in spite of has of) · ✗ Due to it was raining, we stayed in. → ✓ Due to the rain / Due to the fact that it was raining · ✗ Regardless the cost, we will go. → ✓ Regardless of the cost

concept.noteHtml: These prepositions belong to formal writing: reports, official letters, news, academic texts. In speech and emails, people say because of, because, although, before instead: Because of the rain instead of On account of the rain. Some style guides say due to should only follow be and owing to should start a phrase. In real British English both are common, so do not worry about it. Prior to and notwithstanding are very formal. US: Americans write in light of, British writers often write in the light of. For although, however and despite in everyday writing, see contrast and reason. For the formal linkers whereas, given that see formal linkers. For time words see for, since, ago.

tables.caption: Formal prepositions and what they mean
head: Preposition
Meaning
Example
Everyday word
rows: The delay was due to snow.
Trains were cancelled on account of the strike.
He lost his job as a result of the closure.
in view of / in the light of
In view of the weather, we stayed in.
Despite the rain, we went out.
Everyone can join, regardless of age.
The plan went ahead, notwithstanding the objections.
With regard to your letter, we can confirm the booking.
In terms of price, the second hotel is better.
I am writing on behalf of the committee.
They moved the piano by means of a crane.
All staff must wear a badge in accordance with company rules.
Please sign in prior to entering.
In addition to the café, there is a shop.

listen.text: The flight was delayed owing to fog.
listen.note: owing to + noun: a reason. Formal; in speech you would say because of.

listen.text: In spite of the cost, they bought the house.
listen.note: in spite of + noun. Never despite of.

listen.text: Everyone is welcome, regardless of age.
listen.note: regardless of + noun: it does not matter.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose what you hear. You can listen twice.

items.text: Owing to the strike, many trains were cancelled.
Everyone can join, regardless of age.
In view of the weather, the match was postponed.
Despite the delay, we arrived on time.
choices: As a result of the delay

items.text: The problem was due to a faulty cable.
Prior to leaving, please lock the door.

rounds.label: 1 · although → despite
rounds.instruction: You hear a clause with although. Say it again with despite and a noun or an -ing form.

rounds.label: 2 · because of → due to
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with be and because of. Say it with due to.

example.prompt: The delay was because of the weather.
example.answer: The delay was due to the weather.

items.prompt: The delay was because of the snow.
items.answer: The delay was due to the snow.

items.prompt: The cancellation was because of the strike.
items.answer: The cancellation was due to the strike.

items.prompt: The problem was because of a faulty cable.
items.answer: The problem was due to a faulty cable.

items.prompt: The accident was because of the fog.
items.answer: The accident was due to the fog.

items.prompt: Her success was because of hard work.
items.answer: Her success was due to hard work.

items.prompt: The mistake was because of a misunderstanding.
items.answer: The mistake was due to a misunderstanding.
